sources.entry: Faved - Handcrafted bookmark manager combining powerful tagging, instant search, and a clean, distraction-free interface. Built for large collections and advanced workflows, optimized for efficiency and ease-of-use. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Faved is a self-hostable, MIT-licensed bookmark manager for large collections, with nested tags, instant search, and a responsive PWA-capable interface.
summary.what_it_does: Faved stores bookmarks with nested tags, so a tag such as Backend can sit under Programming Languages. It automatically fetches titles, descriptions, and preview images when a bookmark is added, and it flags duplicates. The interface offers instant search, sorting, card/list/table layouts, and bulk actions such as deleting, refetching, and tagging. Users can import bookmarks from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge while keeping folder structure as nested tags, and migrate from Raindrop.io and Pocket. Saving is possible through a Chrome extension, a browser bookmarklet, or Apple Shortcuts. The README says all data is stored locally when self-hosted, with no external dependencies. A hosted cloud option is also offered.
use_cases: organize large sets of saved links
import browser bookmarks with folder structure
save links from iOS share sheet
tag and search saved web pages
how_to_run: Self-host with the Docker setup described in the Installation docs (the README does not include commands)
notable: Nested tags with color, descriptions, rollup to child tags, and pinning
Imports browser folders as nested tags and migrates from Pocket and Raindrop.io
Browser bookmarklet and Apple Shortcuts integration without requiring an extension
Installable as a PWA with system-synced light and dark mode
caveats: Automated tagging is planned, not yet available
Tag icons are marked as coming soon
Cloud hosting is offered as a paid-style managed option; the README does not give pricing
